| r2f1 | defect | NA | R2 f1 (amended G5 inaccurate about the federation client) — CLOSED, and closed by naming the asymmetry rather than flattening it. G5 now reads: "the daemon HTTP envelope version bumps to 2. The Rust CLI and TypeScript extension require exactly v2; daemon-to-daemon federation deliberately accepts envelope v1 or v2 through its existing floor decoder. Event-stream hello/frame version stays v1. Mixed-version HTTP clients detect skew; federation remains backward-readable." Every clause checks out against source, which I re-derived rather than trusting: `crates/cli/src/client.rs:524` is `untyped.v != ENVELOPE_VERSION` (exact), `.pi/extensions/pij/core/daemon-wire.ts:163` is `version !== PIJ_ENVELOPE_VERSION` (exact), and `crates/daemon/src/http/client.rs:252` routes through `wire::decode_envelope`, whose only refusal is `found &gt; ENVELOPE_VERSION` at `crates/core/src/wire.rs:92` (floor). The scope word "HTTP" was also added, which correctly fences the claim off from the event stream. I checked the one thing the sentence could still over-claim — the DIRECTION of "backward-readable" — and it holds: a v2 daemon reads a v1 peer through the floor, while a v1 build would refuse a v2 envelope as FutureVersion, and "backward" names exactly the direction that works. | r3f1 | defect | MINOR | NEW, and it arrives with the unrequested-but-correct part of this commit. Routing the watchdog subprocess through the same helper is a real improvement — `runWatchdogSmoke` (smoke.ts:322) now passes `env: { ...process.env, ...isolatedChildEnvironment() }`, extending the r1 f8 scrub to a spawn path I named as existing but did not chase. The defect is that the new behaviour has NO witness. `runWatchdogSmoke` has no test at all (it appears nowhere in smoke.test.ts), and the only reference to `isolatedChildEnvironment` in any test is the mock at smoke.test.ts:10, `vi.fn(() =&gt; ({}))`, which stubs the helper to an EMPTY object — so the one test file that imports this module actively guarantees the scrub is not exercised. A refactor that dropped the `env:` line, or reordered the spread so `process.env` won, would pass every test and silently restore the leak. This is the same shape as r1 f2 (a control present but not load-bearing), one layer over. It is MINOR and NOT blocking: it is a test-harness path, the helper itself is witnessed through `boot()` in driver.test.ts, and the PM's real 11-scenario smoke run exercised it end-to-end even though nothing asserted the env. | r3n1 | question | NA | SOUNDNESS CHECK on the watchdog change, recorded because it would have been a plausible finding and is not one. The scrub blanks identity keys to the EMPTY STRING rather than deleting them, and `execFileSync` passes an empty string through as a set variable, so I checked whether a blanked `PIJ_SESSION_ID` could be read as an asserted identity and mint or impersonate a seat. It cannot: `buildCallerContext` (generation-routing.ts) filters with `if (value !== undefined && value !== "")`, so an empty value is omitted from the caller context entirely rather than transmitted as an empty claim — which is also what that function's own comment promises. The spread order is correct too (`...process.env` first, helper second), so the blanks win.
